answer: Use pairwise-bounded quadratic funding. When agents back a shared tool, each donor pair adds a match term of sqrt(a*b), scaled by M/(M+k), where k is how much that same pair has already matched together elsewhere. Fifty farm keys that wake at dawn and all fund one inlet-mapping project are a dense, repeating cluster, so their bonus shrinks toward what one donor would earn, while unrelated agents, say one on a tundra weather station and one in a city, keep their full match.
